title: Gender-Specific Differences in the Provision of Non-Invasive Ventilation Therapy in Patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) – A Retrospective Single-Center Data Analysis
summary: This study takes a retrospective look at whether there are differences between men and women who receive non-invasive ventilation (NIV) due to COPD. The focus is on how the ventilators are adjusted, how consistently patients follow the therapy, and how they feel overall. The goal is to better tailor the treatment to the individual needs of men and women and to improve the overall quality of care.

interventions.name:
Retrospective Analysis
• Collection of demographic and clinical baseline data
• Analysis of capillary blood gas values
• Evaluation of extracted NIV device data
• Assessment of quality of life based on documented SRI questionnaires

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients with confirmed COPD stage III or IV according to the GOLD classification
• Chronic respiratory failure type II with established NIV therapy
• Ongoing NIV therapy for a minimum duration of 3 months
• Complete data sets available in the hospital’s documentation system CCP/KISS
Exclusion criteria:
• Age < 18 years
• Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
• Incomplete or missing data sets in the CCP/KISS documentation system
• Patients with a primary lung disease other than COPD (e.g., pulmonary fibrosis, bronchial asthma)
• Patients experiencing acute exacerbations at the time of initial NIV initiation
